newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Communist Vietnam silent on news of Deng's death.
newsitem.headline: Communist Vietnam silent on news of Deng's death.

text.p: China's communist neighbour Vietnam remained silent in the early hours of Thursday morning as news of the death of paramount leader Deng Xiaoping began filtering across the capital, Hanoi.
Outside Beijing's diplomatic compound there was no sign of reaction to be seen. Embassy lights were turned out and local police patrols said they had not been informed that Deng had died.
Flags throughout the city's main diplomatic quarter and area around the Ho Chi Minh mausoleum remained at full mast and state media carried no immediate mention of the news.

Diplomats and analysts said that while Deng Xiaoping's death was expected to have few immediate consequences for Hanoi, the longer-term shockwaves from any political aftermath in China could be profound.
The pragmatic reforms that Deng inspired in China swept south through Vietnam during the mid 1980s where they were officially adopted through a home-grown version known as 'Doi Moi', or renovation.
More than a million people in Vietnam are ethnic Chinese.

Despite a history of mistrust, including a brief and bloody border war in 1979, ties are seen as having warmed in recent years with a growing number of top-level exchanges between the communist neighbours.
